comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1185 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1185), commit
b7e4b6f190, based on main bc9b8a9968.

=== THE RUNTIME FINDING THAT DECIDED THE IMPLEMENTATION ===
`Retry-After` is read from `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`. Verified against
pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 at RUNTIME rather than assumed: `JIRAError.__init__` does
`self.headers = kwargs.get("headers", None)` and its own docstring describes that kwarg as
"will be used to get REQUEST headers". The RESPONSE headers — the ones carrying `Retry-After` —
hang off `.response`. Reading `.headers` would look right, type-check, and silently never find
the header, degrading every 429 to "no header present". The test's fake plants a DECOY
`Retry-After: 9999` on `.headers`, so an implementation that reads the wrong attribute produces
a ~9999s delay and fails loudly instead of passing by coincidence.

=== AC-BY-AC ===
[429 + header retried on an opted-in READ, jittered and clamped, asserted numerically]
`test_an_opted_in_read_retries_a_429_using_the_response_header` asserts three attempts and that
each delay lies in [2.0, 2.4] for a `Retry-After: 2` — i.e. the header value plus up to 20%.
[parse_retry_after / MAX_BACKOFF_S REUSED] Both imported from `_errors`; no second parser and no
second constant. The delay ARITHMETIC deliberately differs from `dispatch_one`'s 429 branch,
which applies no jitter — recorded in the code as a divergence, not copied by accident.
[cap exhaustion raises BackendHTTPError code 429, JIRAError does not escape]
`test_cap_exhaustion_raises_the_neutral_error_and_never_the_vendor_type` asserts BOTH halves.
[EVERY mutation still fails on the FIRST 429, enumerated not sampled] Ten members driven through
the real transport: create_issue, update_issue, add_comment, add_label, remove_label,
transition_issue_by_name, set_relationship, delete_issue, delete_issue_link, set_parent. Asserted
on CLIENT CALL COUNT per member — an implementation that retried and then re-raised would satisfy
a raises-only assertion having issued the write twice.
[opt-in defaults to OFF on all three seams] Asserted for `_with_connection_retry`, `_call_logged`
and `_paged_search` separately.
[_call_logged ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS] Done, and it was a real EDIT: it previously called
`_with_connection_retry(fn)` with no keyword at all.
[_paged_search accepts and forwards, does NOT pass True unconditionally] Done.
[ALL FOUR opted-in read sites pass True, asserted PER SITE] get_issuelinks_map, get_comment_map's
`_paged_search`, get_comment_map's inner PER-ISSUE fetch, get_parent_map.

=== FOUR MUTATION CHECKS, ALL CAUGHT ===
 1. read `exc.headers` instead of `exc.response.headers` -> 2 failed.
 2. `_call_logged` stops forwarding (PATH A) -> 2 failed.
 3. per-issue comment fetch stops opting in (PATH B) -> 1 failed.
 4. clamp BEFORE jitter instead of after -> `test_the_delay_is_clamped_to_max_backoff` fails with
    "delay 68.25 exceeds MAX_BACKOFF_S=60.0".
NOTE ON #4: my first batch run reported it as NOT caught. That was a false negative in my own
harness (stale bytecode between rapid mutate/restore cycles), not a weak assertion — re-run in
isolation with `__pycache__` cleared it fails exactly as intended. Recording it because "the
mutation did not go red" is normally a signal to strengthen the test, and acting on it here would
have been wrong.

=== WHY PATH B EXISTS — the plan-review finding that improved the design ===
Round 1 of this plan threaded the flag through `_call_logged` alone and was BLOCKED for it. The
reviewer was right: `get_comment_map` fetches comments one request PER ISSUE via a DIRECT
`_with_connection_retry` call that bypasses `_call_logged` entirely. That is the highest-volume
read in a pass and therefore the single most likely thing to trip a token bucket — and it was
precisely the call the one-path design could not reach. A rate-limit fix that misses the read
most likely to be rate limited, with every `_paged_search` test passing.

=== GATES === 89 DC unit tests pass (10 new). `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.
transport.py 706 lines, retry.py 235 — both under the locked 800 cap.

compiled_state.description:
# S2 — honour `Retry-After` on 429, scoped to IDEMPOTENT READS

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260] (ten BLOCK rounds; full record on that ticket). S2 is the
POLICY half; [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) was the mechanical relocation that made room for it.
**S1 HAS LANDED** — Gerrit 1179, on `main` as commit `529e802da0`. `transport.py` is now 683 lines
(117 of headroom under the locked 800 cap) and the retry cluster lives in
`adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`. **Every line citation in this plan was re-probed against that
post-S1 tree**; the previous revision's citations were taken pre-S1 and were all stale, which is
what a round of review correctly caught.

Jira Data Center has built-in rate limiting (8.6+, **DC only**, **OFF BY DEFAULT** — an admin
enables it), a per-user token bucket. rebar's DC transport does not handle it:
`_with_connection_retry` retries only connection-level faults and its docstring states that
`jira.exceptions.JIRAError` — any HTTP 4xx/5xx — is NOT in the retry set, so a 429 propagates as a
hard failure on the first occurrence, on an instance that was merely asking rebar to slow down.

Two constraints shape the whole fix:
1. **A static pacing policy is NOT implementable.** The limit is admin-configured and may be absent
   entirely (pre-8.6, Server, or simply disabled), so honour headers WHEN PRESENT and degrade
   gracefully when absent.
2. **Atlassian prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter**, which differs from ADR-0036's
   backoff curve (designed for transient connectivity, where the server offers no guidance).
   Jitter is not decoration: every rebar instance hitting the same bucket would otherwise retry in
   lockstep.

**VERIFY THE NUMBERS BEFORE BUILDING TO THEM** — "off by default", "8.6+" and "retry-after + 20%
jitter" come from OSS research with Atlassian citations, not from testing, and that research
retracted two of its other claims on a second pass.

## Approach

**Reuse what exists — do not build a third `Retry-After` implementation.**
`_errors.parse_retry_after()` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` already exist, `dispatch_one.py:41`
already imports both, and `dispatch_one.py:148-172` is ALREADY a 429-honouring retry path for the
REST transport. Read that path first and mirror it; a second parser is the finding that opened
round 1.

**MIRROR IT, BUT NOT EXACTLY — one deliberate divergence, stated so it is not read as a slip.**
That existing path applies `min(MAX_BACKOFF_S, retry_after)` with **no jitter** on the
`Retry-After` branch (it jitters only the ADR-0036 curve, `dispatch_one.py:167-169`). Atlassian
prescribes `Retry-After` PLUS up to 20% jitter for the DC token bucket, so this story's 429 branch
jitters where the existing one does not. Reuse the PARSER and the CONSTANT; do not copy the delay
arithmetic verbatim.

**SCOPE THE RETRY TO IDEMPOTENT READS. This is the load-bearing constraint.**
`_with_connection_retry` is the single choke point for ALL 15 transport call sites INCLUDING
`create_issue`, `add_comment` and `add_label`, and its docstring already records why JIRAError is
unretried: "retrying a mutation on an HTTP error risks duplicates". Retrying 429s there would
**reintroduce the duplicate-issue class [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] just fixed** — a 429 can arrive
after the server began the write, and nothing in the response distinguishes that from rejection at
the gate. So: per-CALL opt-in, **defaulting to OFF**, so a mutation added later cannot inherit the
retry by omission.

**THE OPT-IN HAS TO REACH THE RETRY LAYER THROUGH TWO DISTINCT PATHS, NOT ONE.** A previous
revision threaded the flag through `_call_logged` alone and was blocked for it; the correction is
recorded here because the gap is invisible unless the call sites are read individually:

  * PATH A — `_paged_search` -> `_call_logged` -> `_with_connection_retry`. `_paged_search`
    (`transport.py:315`) issues its search through `_call_logged` (`transport.py:165`), which today
    calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with **no keyword argument at all**. So `_call_logged` is an
    EDIT TARGET, not merely a conduit: it must accept `rate_limit_retry` and forward it. Omitting
    it makes the flag a no-op that still type-checks.
  * PATH B — a DIRECT `_with_connection_retry` call that bypasses `_call_logged` entirely.
    `get_comment_map` fetches comments **one request per issue** at `transport.py:367`
    (`_with_connection_retry(lambda k=key: self._client.comments(k))`). That is the
    HIGHEST-VOLUME read in a pass and therefore the single most likely thing to trip a token
    bucket — and it is precisely the call PATH A does not reach. It opts in directly.

Getting only PATH A would ship a rate-limit fix that misses the read most likely to be rate
limited, while every test written against `_paged_search` passed.

**WHAT ESCAPES WHEN THE CAP IS EXHAUSTED.** `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, never the raw
`JIRAError`. This is not a preference: it is what the boundary already does.
`_with_connection_retry` (now `retry.py:121`) catches the library error types and raises
`_as_backend_http_error(exc) from exc`, which reads `.status_code` into `BackendHTTPError.code`
using urllib's spelling SO THAT the core's existing `except urllib.error.HTTPError` branches
classify a DC failure exactly as they classify a Cloud one. Leaking `JIRAError` past that boundary
is the actual regression risk here, and J10 pinned the neutral exception contract precisely to stop
it. (A library error with no usable status degrades to `code=0`, which no core branch mistakes for
a 404 or a success.)

## Scope

Four files' worth of edits, and the opted-in read call sites are ENUMERATED HERE — this is the
single enumeration in the document, and Testing and the ACs refer back to it rather than restating
it. (The previous revision had Scope defer to Testing while Testing deferred to Scope, so neither
listed anything; that circularity was a blocking finding.)

- `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — `_with_connection_retry` gains
  `rate_limit_retry: bool = False`; the 429 branch, `Retry-After` parsing, jitter-then-clamp.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`:
  - `_call_logged` (`:165`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and FORWARDS it. Without this
    edit the flag cannot reach the retry layer from `_paged_search` at all.
  - `_paged_search` (`:315`) — gains `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` and forwards it to
    `_call_logged`. It **accepts and forwards**; it does NOT pass `True` unconditionally.

**THE OPTED-IN READ CALL SITES — FOUR, exhaustively** (line numbers probed on `main` at
`529e802da0`, i.e. post-S1):
  1. `get_issuelinks_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:349` — passes `True`.
  2. `get_comment_map` -> `self._paged_search(...)` at `transport.py:363` — passes `True`.
  3. `get_comment_map`'s inner PER-ISSUE comment fetch at `transport.py:367` — a direct
     `_with_connection_retry` call (PATH B above) — passes `True`.
  4. `get_parent_map` -> `self._paged_search(query, fields="parent")` at `transport.py:461` —
     passes `True`.

**NOT in scope:** any mutation call site; any change to ADR-0036's connectivity backoff curve; any
read not in the list of four above (every other read keeps today's behaviour, which is what the
default-OFF flag guarantees).

## Testing

* **the cap-exhaustion contract** — a client that returns 429 forever: assert the escaping
  exception is `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, AND assert `jira.exceptions.JIRAError` does
  NOT escape. A test that only checks "it raised" passes while the vendor type leaks.
* **`Retry-After` is honoured when present** — the sleep is driven by the header, not the ADR-0036
  curve; jitter is applied and the result is CLAMPED to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`.
* **absent header degrades gracefully** — no header (limiter off / pre-8.6 / Server) behaves exactly
  as today.
* **MUTATIONS DO NOT RETRY, enumerated rather than sampled** — assert one 429 fails immediately for
  EVERY non-opting mutation member of the transport. Enumerate them explicitly; an ellipsis is how
  a later-added mutation silently inherits the retry.
* **the opt-in defaults to OFF** — a call that does not pass the flag does not retry a 429.
* **BOTH PATHS carry the flag** — one test per path, because they fail independently: a
  `_paged_search`-driven read (PATH A, exercising the `_call_logged` forward) and
  `get_comment_map`'s per-issue fetch (PATH B, the direct call). A single test over
  `_paged_search` would pass while the highest-volume read remained unprotected.
* **`_call_logged` still forwards nothing by default** — its existing callers (every other
  transport member) must be unaffected, asserted rather than assumed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] [rebar:f2f3-9cb1-335b-4e31] (S1) has LANDED — Gerrit 1179, `main` commit `529e802da0`;
      `transport.py` 789 -> 683 lines, `retry.py` created at 162 lines
- [ ] a 429 with a `Retry-After` header is retried on an opted-in READ, with jitter applied and the
      delay clamped to `MAX_BACKOFF_S`, asserted numerically
- [ ] `_errors.parse_retry_after` and `_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` are REUSED — a test or the diff shows
      no second parser and no second constant
- [ ] cap exhaustion raises `BackendHTTPError` with `code == 429`, and a test asserts `JIRAError`
      does not escape the adapter boundary
- [ ] EVERY mutation call site still fails on the FIRST 429 — asserted per member over an explicit
      enumeration of the transport's mutation members, not a sample
- [ ] the opt-in parameter defaults to OFF on `_with_connection_retry`, on `_call_logged` and on
      `_paged_search`, asserted, so a future call inherits no retry by omission
- [ ] `_call_logged` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry`. This is an EDIT, not a pass-through
      that already works: today it calls `_with_connection_retry(fn)` with no keyword argument, so
      without this change the flag is a no-op that still type-checks
- [ ] `_paged_search` ACCEPTS AND FORWARDS `rate_limit_retry: bool = False` — it does NOT pass
      `True` unconditionally. The decision, not a requirement to decide: an unconditional `True`
      would silently grant retry to every FUTURE caller of the helper, the same "inherits by
      omission" hazard the per-call opt-in exists to prevent
- [ ] ALL FOUR opted-in read call sites listed in Scope pass `True`, asserted PER SITE — including
      `get_comment_map`'s inner per-issue fetch, which does NOT route through `_paged_search` or
      `_call_logged` and is the highest-volume read in a pass
- [ ] the three researched numbers (DC-only, 8.6+, off-by-default; retry-after + up to 20% jitter)
      are each either confirmed against the target DC version or explicitly marked unverified
compiled_state.title: S2 — honour Retry-After on 429, scoped to idempotent reads
